thread:
mia_support: @jordan_billing escalating a customer billing question from Acme Corp. They were billed ~72.5 reserved GPU-hours on 2026-03-10 but their token dashboard shows ~1.2k tokens for the day and no sustained jobs. They say no loadtests. Ticket INC-3142.

sam_customer: Confirm — spike around 02:12 UTC. We didn't run anything. Invoice INV-2026-03-10-ACME shows the GPU-hours.

jordan_billing: Can you DM me the account id + invoice pdf? Region?

mia_support: DM sent. Region: us-west-2.

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] 2026-03-10T02:10:45Z pool 'dedicated-acme' scaled up 0 -> 6 instances (policy min_ready=2, warmup_probe=true).

owen_infra: Autoscaler up -> 6 would explain hours if instances stayed up. Need to check whether these were warmup probes only vs actual customer traffic. Sam, any deploys or traffic you recall?

sam_customer: No deploys. We captured one probe header on our ingress: 'X-Redwood-Warmup: 1' and request-id r-9f8a7c. No other traffic.

lisa_engineering: Hypothesis: prewarm/compile step runs on first boot (10-20m) and currently counts as billed GPU time. Also there's a recent metering edge-case where warmup probes keep an instance in 'active' state until heartbeat timeout (15m).

mia_support: Customer provided repro snippet they observed:
```bash
# example warmup probe seen by customer
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Redwood-Warmup: probe' \
  https://dedicated.us-west-2.redwood.inf/v1/health
```
They only saw a couple of probes but invoice shows much more.

owen_infra: Can infra pull instance lifecycle (instance_id, start_time, terminate_time) + pool config (prewarm flags)? Also check metering-agent logs around 02:00-03:00 UTC.

autoscale-bot: [probe-detector] warmup label detected on 6 boot events for 'dedicated-acme' between 2026-03-10T02:09:30Z and 02:12:05Z; all terminated at 2026-03-10T02:40:17Z.

lisa_engineering: If each instance ran ~28-30m and we billed as full GPU-hours per instance improperly (rounding bug), that could inflate billed hours. There's a PR referencing similar behavior: https://git.redwood/s/repro/warmup-metering-2026 (internal).

jordan_billing: If infra confirms misbilling, we'll open adjustment and SLA credit. Sam, we'll keep you posted.

owen_infra: Pulling lifecycles + hourly aggregates now. ETA ~25m.

mia_support: Customer would like SLA credit if this was platform-initiated. Keeping them in the loop.

sam_customer: Thanks — predictable committed hours are critical for us.

lisa_engineering: Next steps: infra to attach instance lifecycles, engineering to validate metering-agent behavior and confirm whether warmup probes were excluded from metering. If bug: hotfix + retro + add internal non-billable warmup tag.

jordan_billing: Opened billing adjustment BA-7892 pending infra confirmation.

owen_infra: Quick update: raw lifecycles show 6 instances with ~28-30m uptime each. I'm pulling hourly rollups to see how that aggregated to 72.5 hours on the invoice (possible duplicate attribution across billing windows).

mia_support: Thanks team — please post timeline and any definitive cause here so I can close INC-3142 with the customer.

[THREAD END]
